gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may lead to exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a strong, adequately budgeted, and operational Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) to track and respond to grievances from target populations

gen_risks.description: Financial management risks may lead to inaccurate or untimely information on project status
gen_risks.mitigation: Update existing financial management manuals, upgrade accounting software, and recruit an external auditor

gen_risks.description: Procurement risks may lead to delays, governance issues, or limited market competition
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, and adopt flexible procurement approaches

gen_risks.description: Environmental risks may lead to community health risks, occupational health and safety risks, or nuisances related to air and noise emissions
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare an Umbrella Environmental and Social Management Framework (U-ESMF) and adapt it to country context
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gen_risks.description: Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) risks may lead to harm to beneficiaries or project staff
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare country-specific Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and SEA risk assessments and develop corresponding SEA Action Plans
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gen_risks.description: Climate change may lead to increased disease transmission risks, healthcare infrastructure damage, or disruptions to essential health services
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate resilience into project design, including green and resilient infrastructure and climate-informed disease surveillance

gen_risks.description: Inadequate health security governance may lead to weak institutional capacities and limited resources for health emergency preparedness and response
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen health security governance through legislation, regulations, and institutional frameworks

gen_risks.description: Limited laboratory capacity may lead to delayed or inaccurate disease diagnosis, hindering effective response to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen laboratory capacity through equipment, training, and quality management systems

gen_risks.description: Inadequate human resources for health may lead to insufficient capacity to respond to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen human resources for health through training, capacity building, and workforce planning

gen_risks.description: Inadequate emergency response mechanisms may lead to delayed or ineffective response to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish functional emergency response coordination mechanisms, including incident management systems and rapid response teams

gen_risks.description: Inadequate health infrastructure may lead to disruptions to essential health services during health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen health infrastructure through rehabilitation, equipment, and climate-resilient design

gen_risks.description: Inadequate supply chain management may lead to stockouts or shortages of essential medical supplies
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen supply chain management through logistics capacity building, procurement planning, and stock management

gen_risks.description: Inadequate risk communication and community engagement may lead to misinformation, mistrust, or inadequate response to health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement effective risk communication and community engagement strategies, including public awareness campaigns and community outreach

gen_risks.description: Inadequate gender considerations may lead to unequal access to health services or inadequate response to gender-specific health needs
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate gender considerations into project design, including gender-sensitive risk assessments, gender-disaggregated data, and gender-specific interventions

gen_risks.description: Inadequate environmental considerations may lead to environmental degradation, health risks, or inadequate response to environmental health emergencies
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate environmental considerations into project design, including environmental impact assessments, environmental management plans, and climate-resilient infrastructure
gen_risks.evidence: Section IV. D. Environmental and Social

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
